rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken pattern for something like the thing implied by context, as in “such clouds.”

example.english: I’ve never seen such clouds before.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mei6 gin3 gwo3 gam2 joeng2 ge3 wan4

rows.note: Use this pattern when “such” intensifies an adjective before a noun, as in “such a good holiday.”

example.english: It’s rare to have such a good holiday.
example.jyutping: gam2 hou2 ge3 gaa3 kei4 zan1 hai6 naan4 dak1

rows.meaning: such as this/that; people like that
rows.note: Use this before a noun for a person or thing of the kind just mentioned, as in 「咁嘅人」 or 「咁嘅嘢」.

example.english: I don't want to meet such people again.
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 soeng2 zoi3 jyu6 dou2 gam3 ge3 jan4

rows.meaning: such as this/that; people like that
rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose standalone equivalent for a state or situation, as in 「人生就係咁」 for “such is life.”

example.jyutping: jan4 sang1 jau5 si4 zau6 hai6 gam3

rows.meaning: such as this/that; people like that
rows.note: Choose this when “such” emphasizes that the person or thing belongs to that particular type or kind.

example.english: I hate such people who are always late.
example.traditional: 我最怕嗰種人成日遲到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zeoi3 paa3 go2 zung2 jan4 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3

rows.meaning: such as this/that; people like that
rows.note: Use this for specific previously mentioned people or things, corresponding to “those such people/things” rather than a general type.

example.english: I don't want to see such people you mentioned earlier again.
example.traditional: 你頭先講嗰啲人，我唔想再見到。
example.jyutping: nei5 tau4 sin1 gong2 go2 di1 jan4 ngo5 m4 soeng2 zoi3 gin3 dou2
